22. Chapter 22

Summary for the Chapter:

Set during 2x21: Resist and 2x22: Nevertheless, She Persisted. Lena will do whatever it takes to fix this mess.

Traveling via electric current was the least weird thing that had happened to Lena in the past twenty four hours, but that wasn’t saying much. 

As soon as they rematerialized, Lena found herself being tackled by someone, and only the familiarity of Jess’ heartbeat stood between her and being thrown through a wall. Lena wrapped her arms around Jess and hugged her back, not allowing herself to properly sink into the embrace and pulling back after only a few seconds. 

“I saw the broadcast - Hector called me as soon as they landed, but he had to go make sure his mom and his roommate and his lizard were okay, so I’ve been here, trying to figure out how to  - ”

“You’ve done well.” 

“Are you okay?” Jess peered up at Lena, who found herself itchy under the gentle scrutiny. “In that transmission, you looked - ”

“I’m fine. You, um, you called my phone?”

“Yeah, well, that’s protocol with crazy mother stuff, right? Make contact, execute a rescue, have said crazy mother arrested. I called, and even though you didn’t pick up, the signal worked, so I knew Livewire could get to you.”

“She’s not - ” Lena let out a breath, dragging her fingers over her scalp, skidding over the intricate braids. “She’s not crazy. She’s entirely in her right mind, and that’s what makes her dangerous. And she’s threatened every hospital in this city, including mine, so Livewire, I need you to take me back.”

“Um.” Livewire crossed her legs, floating on a crackling cloud of electricity and arching one eyebrow. “No?”

“Um, yes.”

“Look, I came and got you because I owed you one and because Jess asked, but that’s the full extent of the favor I owed you. I’m not taking you back there so you can enact your own little self-flagellatory suffering. You’re out, you’re welcome, Jess and I are going back to Belize.”

“Like hell we are.” Jess set her jaw and braced her hands on her hips. “You can go, if you want to, but you’re putting her back first.”

“Are you kidding me? You’ve never been held hostage, you don’t know what it’s like!” Livewire touched down, the toes of her heavy boots grazing the floor, and hissed, “You didn’t see her up there, Jess.”

Jess glanced over at Lena, dark eyes shining with worry. She set her jaw, turning back towards Livewire, and said, “I trust Lena. And I’m not going anywhere until she gets what she asked for.”

Livewire ran her fingers through her hair, electricity crackling through the pale strands and standing them on end, and pivoted on her heel, pacing up through the air. “Baudelaire?”

Lena tightened her fingers in her skirt, crumpling the fabric into fists. “She’s going to use L Corp to drug the water supply. I need your help - both of your help - to stop her on the ground while I keep her placated on the ship.”

“What?”

“She’s going to take control of the company and use it to manufacture some kind of psychotropic to make everyone complacent, and then she’s going to enslave you. All of you. If you can block her - ”

Jess’ brows furrowed, briefly, before a slow smile crept hesitantly across her face. “That’s… not a problem.”

“What do you mean?”

“Um, Arias, from accounting, she’s thrown so much red tape around the controlling seat that you might have a hard time getting back into it.”

Lena let out a breath she hadn’t known she’d been holding, slumping forward, shoulders shaking. “Is she safe?”

“Did it all from her couch with her kid.”

“Thank god,” Lena laughed, vision blurring. She straightened up with a sharp inhalation, wiping her eyes. “All that’s left is getting some information to Supergirl and grabbing some lead.”

“Are you gonna make some cheap toys? Paint a few walls? Poison babies?”

“Queen’s not a baby.” A hiccuping sob crept out of Lena and she shook her head.“Lead is toxic to Daxamites.”

Jess’ eyes widened. “Aren’t you a - ?”

Lena snapped into motion, unzipping the tiny pocket she’d made in her bodice and pulling out the nano bot.

“I was wondering what MacGuffin ex machina you were pulling out of your ass,” Livewire said, eyeing it. “And the walls.”

With a soft smile, Lena eyed the bot in her palm. “This has all the information on the ship’s mainframe - ship’s logs, personal data, the invasion plans. There should be enough storage space in here for - for everything important. I need you to get that to the D.E.O.. J’onn, Lucy, Alex, or - ” Lena cut herself off, eyes shut tight. 

“Got it.”

“Don’t tell them it came from me, or they won’t trust that information. Jess, I need you to load the data onto a private server so, if push comes to shove, we - you - can give everyone the information they need to defend themselves.”

Jess nodded sharply and took the bot, squeezing Lena’s hand. “Protect yourself, okay? With the lead.”

Lena offered no promise but a weak smile and took off for storage. There wasn’t much use for lead, so there wasn’t much kept on site, but she had more than enough to tip her knuckle dusters and form a short blade. 

At first, she didn’t bother with gloves, and maybe it was only pure habit that made her reach for the stuff with her bare hands. The lead burned on contact, the same way Lillian’s chains had, the same way the capsule embedded in Kara’s chest had, and it took her a moment too long to withdraw. She gritted her teeth, pulled on a pair of welding gloves, and went back to work. It took only seconds to tear off enough lead to complete her task, but it was time enough for Livewire to appear behind her with a telltale crackle.

“You don’t have to go back.”

“Yes, I do.”

“For who?”

“I have to protect everyone she might hurt.”

“Bullshit.”

“Just because you,” Lena said, voice razor-thin as she turned to face Livewire, “are beholden to no one and don’t give a shit about anyone doesn’t mean we all have that luxury. I brought them here. I put people at risk. Every second I’m not up there is a second more innocent people die. I - I have to make up for everything that’s been lost because of me.”

Livewire popped her wrists, electricity crackling at her fingertips, and floated over a piece of metal for a hilt.“You’re running away.”

“And I’m taking them with me.” Lena pinched and pulled the lead into a short, wicked blade, carefully not meeting Livewire’s gaze. Instead, she eyed the metal - shimmery, deep purple marionite. “All of them.”

“This is what’s wrong with you hero types,” Livewire huffed, soldering the blade to the hilt with a fingertip. “You’re so full of self-sacrificial self loathing, you never consider that the people you’re leaving behind might have shittier lives in your absence.”

“You’re talking about - ” Lena cut herself off with a convulsive gulp.

“You can’t even say her name.”

“I brought destruction to her home. I’m - I’m her worst enemy, on a cellular level! It’s not just a Luthor and a Super, okay? She got past that, because that’s tiny, petty bullshit compared to millennia of blood feuding, but all that blood feuding is in my blood. If she’s going to hate me, I’d rather do something good while avoiding her.” 

She snatched back the knife and balanced it in her hands before tucking it, and the rest of the lead, away in her jerry-rigged pocket before starting back up the stairs.

Jess was leaning over her desk, brows furrowed, focus intense. She looked up when Lena walked in, Livewire already at her side with her feet propped up next to the monitor, and stood back.  “Time to go?”

“Do you have everything set up?”

“How long do you want me to wait before releasing?”

Lena thought for barely a second. “Give me three days.”

Jess typed in a few vicious keystrokes, then looked Lena’s way again. “Done.”

“Call it in.”

Jess dialed Lena’s number, and once they heard the first ring, Livewire grabbed Lena’s hand and phased into the current. They were back on Rhea’s ship before the tone had cut off.

Lena let go of Livewire’s hand more reluctantly than she’d have liked to admit, striding over to her discarded tiara and picking it up, clutching it nervously to her chest.

Livewire stared her down for a long moment before shaking her head. “The D.E.O.’s gonna question where I got that information.”

“I don’t care what you tell them, so long as they take it.”

“And when Prom Queen asks about you? She’s not half as dumb as I wish she was.”

Lena opened her mouth, hesitating. “Tell her I’m sorry.”

Livewire zapped away, somehow managing to make the crackle of electricity sound disappointed, and Lena was alone again.

Not for long, though. Her door melted open, and all Lena had the energy to think was at least it isn’t Rhea.

Instead, it was Mon-El. 

“This is your fault, you know.”

She blinked, feeling strangely as if she’d missed something, remembering only too late that she was wearing welding gloves. She dropped the circlet in her haste to hide her hands, and it clattered jarringly to the floor.

“You, being here. You sent out a distress call. We were going to leave, and you sent out an S.I.S. - ”

Lena cringed. “S.O.S.”

Mon-El leaned against the doorframe and clenched his jaw. “The point is, two months ago, you sent out a distress call, and we stayed. Mother just had to have you.”

“Two months ago…” Lena counted back, then laughed. “Two months ago? I was being held against my will by my - by Lillian Luthor. She tried to stick a needle into my brain stem, and Rhea’s little dampener threw her across the room. I didn’t even know she existed.”

Rolling his eyes, Mon-El said nothing.

“I’ve done the whole sibling inadequacy thing before, and it isn’t worth the repeat. I didn’t ask for any of this. I didn’t ask to be some… experiment, I didn’t ask to be kidnapped or manipulated or threatened, and I certainly didn’t ask for yet another mother to see me as sub-par or another brother to disappoint me.”

“Do you think I asked for a sister? Or to end up on Earth, to actually be sub-par? I’m not equipped to be anything other than the heir, and now I can’t even do that, because of you.”

Now it was Lena’s turn to ooze derision. “Trust me, if I thought you were capable of making things better, I’d cede power in a second, but if this is anyone’s fault, it’s - ”

Yours.

The thought was enough of a shock that it stopped Lena cold. Because, yes, it almost was his fault. If she had never met him, that day at CatCo when all she wanted was to ask her friend on a fucking date, the gene suppressor would never have been triggered, and she would have been Lena Luthor, human, forever. 

But he hadn’t sought her out. He hadn’t fled a dying planet with hopes to ruin the life of a person who hadn’t even been born yet, or implanted something in her fucking spine.

No, that was all Rhea.

“Look,” Lena said, shoulders sinking, “I don’t - I don’t have the energy to fight you, or to give a shit that you hate me. We’re both stuck here. We can avoid each other, or we can try to get along. I know what I’d rather do - ”

“Avoid each other?”

Dryly, Lena smiled, and said, “Absolutely. Get the hell out.”

Mon-El started out of the threshold, then paused, turning back to look at her. “I would have been good at it. Being king of Old Daxam.”

“From what I’ve seen - drugging your subjects, experimenting on children, invading and enslaving - that’s not something to be proud of.” 

If those whispery doors could slam, they would have behind him. 

Lena sank back onto the bed, hunching over her knees with her back to the entrance. She plucked the lead dagger from her dress, letting it dangle by the hilt from her fingers, just watching the artificial lights glisten off the keen edge. 

She set the knife down and bit down on the fingertips of her gloves, pulling them off and tucking them under the pillow before picking the dagger back up and rising to her feet. She took a few practice swipes and jabs, trying to picture Rhea. If their clothes were anything alike, her bodices would be reinforced to the point that the knife would be useless, which meant Lena had to go for the throat.

Lena didn’t know if she could.

☆

With no real way to tell the time, Lena couldn’t be sure when exactly Rhea summoned her, especially since, at some point, she’d fallen asleep. Thankfully this time she woke up in what she’d conked out in, but there were the two women again, waiting with a change of clothes. 

She stifled a shocked noise at the sight of two people standing over her in her sleep and scrambled to find the knife. Thankfully, it had migrated under her hip, and stayed hidden when she sat up. 

“Her Majesty is waiting for you in the throne room.”

“I’ll be out shortly,” Lena promised, accepting the clothes. She wondered if it was Rhea’s attempt to mend fences, coordinating them with her armor, and began to dress herself without thinking. Only when she had peeled out of her dress’ bodice did she see her tiny zipper and think better. 

Even if she never went back, Galaxy Girl existed to protect National City - to protect everyone who called the planet Earth their home. Galaxy Girl was Lena’s decision, independent of all machinations and greater plans.

Galaxy Girl could kill Rhea. 

Lena emptied the pocket, reclaiming the baton she’d fashioned into a zipper, and pulled on her suit. Tucking her knife and Kara’s note into her pockets, she gave herself a once-over and wrapped the purple cloak around herself. With her cowl down, it was impossible to tell what she had planned; with her gloves on, the lead knuckles couldn’t burn her. 

She had only just managed to slip them on when two guards burst in.

“You’re lucky I’m finished,” she said sharply, tugging the cloak more surely shut as she whipped around to face them. “You couldn’t have waited for me to walk out on my own?”

They both looked immediately, if reluctantly, cowed. Lena marked the guns on their hips and squared her jaw. She started towards the door, but neither of them moved out of her path.

“You’re, um, you’re forgetting something?”

Tiara. Right. 

Lena carefully settled it on her head, then pushed past the two guards and into the hall. Only a few feet on, she saw Mon-El, also flanked by armed guards. 

He might be a hiccup, Lena thought. He’s been on Earth long enough to have some serious solar reserves, and he seems to actually want Rhea to love him.

I could beat him in a fight. I’ve done it before. But it’s the timing that’s the problem. How do I incapacitate him and commit regicide - matricide - whatever before someone might think to stop me?

Lena began calculating, plotting out a timeline in her head that could compensate for the added obstacle, and had only just reached the third unsuccessful iteration in her head when a flash of purple light spat out three familiar faces.

Immediately, the four armed guards had their weapons raised, aimed squarely at Supergirl, Hank Henshaw, and Lillian Luthor.

“Weapons down, now.”

Their resolves didn’t even falter.

“As your queen,” Lena said, voice clipped, “I order you to lay your weapons down.”

“We are charged with protecting the royal family.”

“Yeah,” Lena said, clenching her jaw, “I’m good.” 

She rammed her elbow back into his throat, slamming him back into the wall so hard she dented it and grabbing his gun by the muzzle with her right hand. She whipped around, pistol-whipping her other guard before switching hands so she had a clearer shot at the two guards charging towards her would-be rescuers, swiftly dispatching them.

Lena knelt down to grab one by his ankle, dragging him back to hide him in her room.  She would figure out how to handle everything once they were awake and Rhea was dead. Once she’d dealt with all four of them, Lena turned towards Mon-El. “I trust you won’t breathe a word of this to Rhea?”

“Wouldn’t dream of it.” He smiled grimly, hands up as he took a slow step backwards. “I’m just gonna head back to my room.”

Satisfied, Lena turned towards the intruders, noting with a shudder the gleam of pride in Lillian’s eyes, and said, “You three.” Her voice shook, barely detectible even to her own hypersensitive ears. “Go. Now. You can’t be seen here, or you’re dead.”

“We came to get you,” Kara replied, rock-solid. “And we’re not leaving without you.”

Lena blinked. After how Kara reacted when Maggie had to arrest her after Lillian’s escape, all those months ago, she never could have imagined her girlfriend one day detaining her. It stung, but she got it.

“Look,” she said, lowering the gun, “normally, I wouldn’t resist arrest. I get it, that you don’t trust me. I wouldn’t trust me either - ”

Kara’s eyes widened. “No, Lena - ”

“ - because I’m one of them, and I didn’t tell you.” Lena’s breath hitched painfully. “But, Kara… Kara, I didn’t - ”

“I knew!”

“ - know!” Then Kara’s words registered. “Wait. What?”

Now it was Kara who approached like she was walking towards a wounded animal. “Rhea made that capsule out of lead, Lena, so the kryptonite wouldn’t affect me until she triggered the release, and so Mon-El couldn’t help me. It burned you when you touched it.”

Lena’s pounding heart roared in her ears. 

“Lena,” Kara said, eyes welling up and voice trembling, “Lena, I knew. I should have told you, and I’m so sorry, but we’re running out of time, we have to go! ”

“It’s okay.” Lena swallowed hard, clutching her batons. “It’s - it’s fine. You don’t…?”

Somehow, Kara knew exactly what she was going to say, and shook her head. “No. I could never hate you. I didn’t tell you because I didn’t want you to ever think I could hate you. And I know you said nothing big until they’re gone, but - ”

Lena shook her head. “They’re going to be gone.” An uncertain smile wobbled at the corners of her mouth. “I’m going to take care of everything, okay? We’re going to leave, and we’ll never come back.”

Kara’s eyes widened, and finally spilled over. “No. No, you can’t.” She rushed to Lena, a rolling storm front. “You can’t, Lena, please!”

“Yes,” Lena murmured, cradling Kara’s face in her hands, “I can.”

“You couldn’t even kill me,” Lillian drawled. “Not with two decades of bad blood between us. How could you ever possibly think you had it in you to kill your real mother?”

“This isn’t about me. Or any one person. This is for the fate of every single living person on Earth, and I can do it for them.” Kara wouldn’t meet her gaze, so Lena ducked down to make her. “Hey, it’s okay. It’s going to be fine. You can go home, okay? You can - you can go home, and be Kara Danvers, and live your life - ”

“No.” Kara’s eyes sizzled. “I’m not just going to abandon you - ”

“You’re not abandoning me. You’re not doing anything wrong.” Lena stretched up on her toes and kissed Kara’s forehead. “Rrip vo nim khap tulem.” 

Lillian’s mouth shifted, turning down at the corners, upper lip curling, and her eyes went tight. “We’re on a tight schedule here. The president is going to destroy this ship, whether we’re on it or not. Is that really necessary?”

Hackles rising, Lena went on the offensive when she realized she’d effectively outed herself to her mother. She wasn’t sure what had put that sickened, mournful expression on Lillian’s face, whether it was the alien language or “Even if this wasn’t the last time I’d ever see her,” Lena hissed, “it would be necessary.”

Kara wrapped her arms around Lena’s waist, pulling her into a tight hug that made her armor creak, planting a kiss on the top of her head. “Ehrosh-bem, i zhor. Voiehd nahn zha ewuhshehd.”

With a wet, hollow laugh, Lena buried her face in Kara’s shoulder, fingers curling around the back of her neck and tangling in her hair. It seemed Kara could sense her disbelief, because she leaned back, just enough to look Lena square in the eyes, before pulling her into a kiss.

“That,” Lena murmured, soaring, “was one hell of a goodbye.”

“Not a goodbye.”

There was a flash of purple light, and both of them turned to look. 

Lillian was gone, and she’d taken Henshaw with her.

“I suppose you’re right,” said Lena faintly.

“Lillian betraying us wasn't the biggest shock ever,” said Kara with a weak smile. “So, Winn bugged Henshaw and rigged a remote so I could beam us back if she double-crossed us.”

“Hope for the best, have Winn Schott prepare for the worst.” Lena dragged Kara into one last hug before stepping away from her. “Use it. Go.”

“Can’t do that just yet.” Kara retrieved something from her uniform’s hidden pocket - a tiny piece of metal, virtually indistinguishable from a ball bearing. “According to this, there’s one more prisoner I have to rescue.”

Lena’s heart gave an impetuous flutter. “Who?”

“Kal-El.”

Shit.

“Get him and get out, okay?” Lena tapped Kara’s collarbone emphatically, peering up at her. “Promise me that saving him is your last heroic deed on board this ship.”

“Pinky - ”

Lena cut Kara off at the sound of footsteps, eyes tight. It took only a moment’s focus more to determine who was coming their way, but it was a moment Lena was afraid to spare.

“Rhea?”

“What do we do?”

Kara set her jaw. “We don’t do anything. You hide.”

“Me hide?”

“Yes, you hide!”

“You’re not even supposed to be here! You need to get your cousin and go!”

“Maybe I - Maybe I can talk her down.”

“I have tried.” Lena shook her head, heart pounding faster than the leisurely footsteps clicking nearer and nearer. “Maybe… maybe not hard enough, but if she won’t listen to me, she’s not going to listen to you, and even if she does, you’re not going to have time to get him and get out alive!”

“She and I both know how it feels,” Kara murmured, “to watch your world burn out. To think you’ve lost everything, to have to scrape together something that feels like home and family. If I were in her shoes, I wouldn’t want to give up, either.”

“But that’s why you can get her to.”

Kara smiled, but it didn’t reach her eyes. “Do you trust me?”

“With everything I am.”

“I trust you, too.” 

Lena nodded, starting for her door, only to pause and fumble with her knuckle dusters, pressing both pairs into her palm. “This’ll help, if it comes to blows.”

Something crossed Kara’s face, an expression Lena didn’t have time to decode, and she took the lead knuckles, trading them for something much smaller. “Think you can get Kal-El off the ship?”

“If he cooperates.”

One of them, or maybe both, dragged the other into a bruising kiss before Lena darted off, too fast to be seen. Her hand curled protectively around the nanobot in her hand, and only then did she remember the tiny change that she had made. 

Lena had adjusted it to project information - that must have been how Kara was planning to find Kal-El and abscond with him unseen. She activated the display and followed the map, swiping past pop-ups and wondering why, for fuck’s sake, there were pop-ups. 

I swear to god, if Jack has a Trojan, I’m going to be pissed at the D.E.O..

Finally, she came to a stop, ricocheting off walls to dispel the excess momentum and landing in front of a wall.

It took a second for her to notice the half-hidden control panel in the wall, a more covert version of the ones that opened and closed all the doors on the ship. All it required was the handprint of someone with access. 

“Fuck it,” Lena muttered, and smashed the glass. She removed her circlet and wedged it into the circular mechanism of the scanner, jamming it. The gears spasmed, and the door slid open to reveal Superman. The veins in his neck glowed a faint silver that crept ever higher, crawling up his jaw like old ivy, and he was restrained by cuffs that anchored directly into the wall. 

Those cuffs were made of a substance with a similar silver glow, and Lena knew immediately that, whatever this was, Rhea had done it to him. 

Slowly, she approached, hands out. “Kal-El?”

He opened his eyes halfway. “Who - where are we?”

“We’re on a ship,” Lena said, taking another step, “but you’re getting off, okay? I just need to get these cuffs off.”

“Cuffs?”

“Yeah.” Lena swallowed nervously. “Do you trust me to do that?”

“Of course,” he mumbled. “We’re family, Kara.”

Lena froze, if only for a heartbeat. Then she sprang back into action, walking behind him to inspect the collar around his neck, avoiding the inevitability of trying to tell him the truth. Once she told him who she was, whatever trance he was under might break, and he wouldn’t let her help him.

It was securely attached to the wall, with no weak points that she could detect. As she inspected the shackles on his wrists, she glanced up at him sporadically, making sure he wasn’t about to flip, finally recognizing her face, and attack. 

The cuffs had to be kryptonite - if Krypton exploded onto Daxam, then there would have been tons of radioactive material raining down, and Rhea would have an almost unlimited supply - which meant Lena couldn’t risk shattering the cuffs, or the kryptonite might enter his bloodstream. She had to get them off another way.

There was a panel, another palm reader, clearly linked to the cuffs’ controls.

Shit.

Lena ducked her head back outside and attempted to pull the tiara out of the other scanner’s inner workings, but it had sort of fused itself to the machinery.

Shit! 

Lena’s hands trembled as she pressed her palm onto the scanner, hoping Kara could forgive her if it went horribly wrong. 

But it didn’t. 

The scanner beeped, a friendly little sound, and the cuffs came off. 

Kal-El beamed, and Lena could see the family resemblance. His face was more angular than Kara’s, sure, but their smiles were the same guileless grins, with the same dimples and the same light. 

“Thank you, Kara,” he said, rubbing his wrists. “Keep an eye out, okay? Zod might be anywhere.”

“You defeated Zod.” Lena rushed to his side when he took his first steps away from the shackles, wobbling only slightly. “Years and years ago. Before Lex went bad.”

Superman didn’t seem to have heard a word she said, but he did allow her to help him out into the hall until he regained his sea legs. “You’re right. We can defeat him together. El mayarah.”

“El mayarah,” Lena parroted grimly. “Let’s get you to to the D.E.O.. They’ll know what to do.”

They moved much more slowly, though Kal-El did eventually find his footing, and soon enough, Lena could hear Kara without using her heightened senses. 

“…while you still have time. The fate of every single living person, every human, every Daxamite, they all rest on the two of us finding peace. Think of them, and let us find it together.”

“Touching speech, Supergirl.” Rhea’s voice was as gentle and resonant as always. 

Lena’s hands clenched into desperate fists at her sides. “Stay quiet, okay?” she whispered, sub-sonic, to Kal-El, who nodded, tossing her a familial wink that hollowed her stomach. The kryptonite wasn’t making him physically weak, so it had to be affecting the sensory input in his brain, corrupting the interpretation of data. That was the only explanation, and it rattled her enough to pull a few feet ahead of Kara’s cousin. 

“Sadly,” Rhea continued, “wasted on the wrong audience.” 

Finally, Lena could see Rhea’s back. She wore no armor, only a simple gown and a thin cape that grazed the floor at her feet. Lena reached into her pocket and wrapped her fingers around the hilt of the blade, preparing to strike.

“When my own husband opposed me, I killed him.You really think you can tug at my heartstrings?” Rhea’s weight shifted, her posture shifting with it into something serpentine, self-satisfied. “You were right about one thing though. It is over. For you.”

Lena locked eyes with Kara and jerked her head, indicating where Kal-El stood, before pulling up her cowl and gripping the dagger tight, targeting the nape of Rhea’s neck. It wasn’t purely for poetic reasons, though the cyclical nature of the act was pleasant; if she could wedge the lead right between C1 and C2, Rhea’s nervous system would be flooded with it, and it would all be over in an instant.

“You really thought you'd won, didn’t you?”

“No,” said Kara, “but for a moment, I hoped we both might.” She squared her shoulders, head back, and held the most intense eye contact with Rhea before she extended her hand and began to speak, this time as if she’d memorized the words, as if they carried true weight. “Queen Rhea of Daxam. I, Supergirl, champion of planet Earth, invoke the sacred rite of Dakkam Ur, to meet with you in single combat before the gods. May the fate of my people rest on the fate of my life.”

 

Rhea seemed to be considering Kara’s offer, almost as if she respected those words, and reached out.

As soon as they clasped hands, Lena was thrown aside, and she lost her grip on the knife. Kal-El barreled past her, charging at Kara, and hit her so hard she slammed through Lena’s doors, roaring, “Stay away from them!”

Lena was moving before she even registered what he’d done, rolling up to her feet and racing towards the last two children of Krypton, only for Rhea to reach out and stop her. 

“She came through our doors, armed with lead,” Rhea murmured, pushing back Lena’s cowl and tucking a stray hair back into her intricate braids. 

No. That was supposed to keep her safe!

“She knew what she risked, crossing me.”

“This is my planet.” Superman grabbed Kara by the arms and threw her down the hall, soaring just out of Lena’s grasp and crashing into a corner so hard the joining walls cracked. “These are my people!”

Kara fumbled for purchase, trying to get on her feet as sparks flew around her, and Lena could hear her panic.

“And I will not let you harm them,” Kal-El snarled, advancing on her once again.

“Don’t!” Lena snagged him by the cape, begging Rhea, “Please, don’t let him hurt her.”

Rhea eyed her, calculating, and the scrutiny was enough to loosen Lena’s grip. Kal-El stepped past her and towards Kara, who found her feet just in time to kick him square in the chest, sending him crashing backwards. 

“You poisoned him,” Kara rasped, leaning heavily against the wall as she stumbled forwards. 

“Very astute. I once told you that my planet was riddled with the corpse of yours. But not only Green Kryptonite rained down from the skies. There are so many more ways to harm your kind than to simply weaken you.” Rhea grinned, all victory and vengeance. “Silver Kryptonite.”

Kara flinched at the mere word, squaring her shoulders - squaring up for a fight.

Rhea rose to her feet, moving between Lena and Kara, almost as if she was protecting her. “Your cousin is so much like you: reckless, stupid, barreling headfirst into danger.” She laughed, her amusement entirely genuine. “I couldn't have set a better trap if I tried.”

Kara peered past Rhea, first to Lena and then to Superman. “Kal,” she managed, “please. It’s me, Kara!”

“Oh, he doesn't see you,” Rhea drawled. “He sees his worst enemy.”

“You should have stayed away, Zod.”

Kara jutted her chin, eyes glistening, and kept trying. “Kal, listen to me.”

Kal-El decided not to listen. He aimed his heat vision at Kara, powering up so fast she barely had time enough to counter the blast. 

“You're his mortal enemy, Supergirl. The person he fears most.You will take everything from him, so, this time, he will not hesitate.This time, he will protect his planet. This time - ”

“I’ll stop you forever,” spat Superman, zooming towards Kara and tackling her. They flew back, through the broken doors, and Lena heard glass shatter.

A split second of Kara plummeting and brawling with her cousin was too much to take; Lena blocked out every sound from below but that of Kara’s thudding pulse, turning her attention towards Rhea.

“What is Dakkam-Ur?” she asked. “I’ve seen that phrase somewhere before.”

“It’s a duel to the death. Whoever wins, reigns.”

Lena’s breath caught in her throat, but her mind zoomed on, snagging on and retrieving a tiny factoid she’d come across when she first started fencing - when she’d first read about Julie D’Aubigny. “There are dueling conventions on Earth. Or, there were. People don’t really duel anymore.”

“Oh?” 

Gleaning that she’d piqued Rhea’s interest, Lena continued. “On Earth, when people dueled, they had seconds to step in for them, to arrange everything in advance so all they had to worry about was winning.”

“She may be the stronger Kryptonian, l’inah, but that isn’t enough for me to grant you - ”

“I’m not offering to be her second,” Lena said, voice somehow steady. “If you accept, I’m offering to be yours… Mother.”

Rhea’s eyes lit up at the word, and she smiled, warm and soft. “L’inah,” she murmured, taking Lena in her arms, “I would like nothing better.”

☆

Whatever happened to the President’s weapon, Olivia Marsdin clearly wasn’t going to blast them out of the sky. Nevertheless, Rhea began to bring the troops back onto their ships, all but emptying the streets of Daxamite forces, and that, in and of itself, was suspicious, but Lena didn’t have the heart to question it. Kara’s life was on the line. Kara could die.

Lena meant it when she said she trusted Kara with everything she was, and she believed Kara could win any fight. She also knew, the way she knew gravity was real or that the majority of her life had been a lie, that Kara would never allow someone to hurt her, which meant not a single Daxamite ship would be fired upon.

Maybe that’s the real reason Rhea brought her soldiers back, Lena mused, so they wouldn’t get hurt. I’m a human shield.

Daxamite shield, rather.

Absently flicking the nanobot’s display on and off, Lena let her head loll back onto the wall behind her where she sat on the floor, unmoving. 

Maybe I should have let Lillian take me back to Earth. I could have figured something out, shielded the city instead of its invaders. Rhea wouldn’t attack if she thought I might get hurt - at least, I don’t think so. But, then, she has Mon-El. He doesn’t fight her.

That’s why she doesn’t try with him. Because she knows he’s already hers. Me, she has to fight for.

Why couldn’t I make her fight harder? Why can’t I bargain for a better fate for Earth?

She waited out the night in dull silence, rolling the nanobot in her fingers, hearing honed resolutely in on Kara and Kal-El’s heartbeats, eyes scanning through everything in the ship’s files until she found Dakkam-Ur. When she’d given Kara all the information on the ship, she’d inadvertently given her the idea to fight Rhea to the death.

. It was like killing Jack all over again, and this time, nothing could thaw her out. She had failed. She couldn’t kill Rhea; she couldn’t uninvade National City; she couldn’t protect Kara or Kal-El or Winn or James or Alex or Maggie or anyone.

Lena kept looking, desperate, for anything that might give Kara an edge. Eventually, Kal-El’s pulse normalized, adrenaline and kryptonite fading, and some time in the early morning, sun barely risen, Kara’s went from sleep to wakefulness. Lena felt a distant flare of hope that soon extinguished itself. 

It was then, when Kara woke up, that Rhea summoned her. This time, she didn’t send guards, but the two cowed women who had given up on trying to dress Lena like some fourteenth century noblewoman. Apparently, she’d surmised that Lena wouldn’t fight someone acting against their own will. 

Or maybe she just didn’t think Lena would fight her any more.

Lena followed them out to the throne room, and Rhea greeted her with a smile. 

“She’s awake.”

“How do you know that?”

“You’re not the only one who can listen, my dear.” Rhea nodded to one of her seemingly endless grunts, and he activated a transmission feed, broadcasting her across the whole city. “Dakkam-Ur. I accept your challenge, Supergirl. My daughter will serve as my second in this duel; send your second to meet her. May the strongest warrior reign everlasting.”

Moments later, a missive arrived, locked by the same code as Lena’s medical file at the D.E.O.. Alex wanted to meet her.

Lena transmatted down to the coordinates in the message - they were in the desert, near that D.E.O. base, and though she’d come alone, Alex hadn’t.

To her right was Lucy; to her left, Kal-El in civilian clothes, immediately recognizable as Clark Kent. Both humans were armed to the teeth, but neither of them reached for their weapons at the sight of her. 

“Figured you’d have company,” Alex said, propping her hands on her hips. 

“It took a good deal of convincing to make sure I didn’t.”

“Digging the cloak,” Lucy interjected coolly. “Very Round Table.”

Lena offered a weak smile, saying nothing.

“When and where?”

“D.E.O. You can hold Rhea if she loses, but doesn’t die, and if Kara - ” Lena’s voice caught in her throat, but she pushed on hoarsely. “If she gets hurt - ”

Alex looked as wrecked by the suggestion as Lena felt, nodding shortly. “Solar noon is at… 1.06p.m. If they fight at, say, half-past, she’ll have enough time to charge up to maximum.”

“She - she needs anti-kryptonite technology, too.” Lena rolled the nanobot between her palms. “Apparently, when Krypton died, it irradiated the atmosphere on Daxam with kryptonite. Everyone who was on the planet when that happened is pumped full of it; if Kara draws blood, she’s at an immediate disadvantage.”

Kal-El eyed her, like he wasn’t quite sure what to make of her, and Lena couldn’t hold his gaze. 

“If we’re done…”

“Wait!”

Lena waited. 

“Your mother - ” Alex paused, correcting herself. “Lillian. She has a backup plan.”

“Something of your brother’s,” Kal-El continued. “It was a bioweapon intended to do exactly what you just described on Daxam, only to Earth - make the atmosphere toxic to Kryptonians. She thinks you can retool it, so it’ll poison Daxamites instead - ”

Lena snorted. At long last, Lillian had finally decided to kill her.

“ - but she’s reluctant to use it.”

“Really.”

Kal-El shrugged, an unassuming gesture, and reached into the lining of his jacket. “It’s your call.”

Lena began reaching for the device, whatever it was, before she had a chance to think. Once her brain caught up to her body, though, she stopped. “I can’t make it work from the ship. I have no access to lead.”

“Your objection to this plan isn’t the whole suicide part,” Lucy asked, incredulous, “but the lack of supplies?” 

“I started this,” said Lena simply. “I have to finish it.”

With that, she cued up the transmat, ready to depart.

As she warped away, she thought she heard Alex apologizing.

Notes for the Chapter:

Kryptonese translations:
Rrip vo nim khap tulem. = I need you to keep existing (literally, you I need to be, future tense - Kryptonian sentence structure is pretty similar to ASL.)
Voiehd nahn zha ewuhshehd. = This is not the end.
Ehrosh-bem = shalom, basically.

Chap. Recap:
Before they leave, Lena loads the ship's mainframe into the nanobot she kept with her. Livewire rescues Lena, and she says it's because she kind of owes her and because Jess made her go, but she genuinely does give a shit about Lena. Lena demands to be sent back, because Rhea is threatening every hospital in the city, and says as much. She also explains about the whole drugging-the-water-supply thing, which is actually not a problem, because one Samantha Arias from Accounting put the kibosh on Rhea taking control of L Corp. Livewire initially refuses, because A) she knows how shitty it is to be kidnapped in general and B) she saw Lena breaking down, trapped up there, and doesn't want to be responsible for that. Jess, however, trusts Lena's judgement, and even though she doesn't want Lena to suffer, she knows it will be worse if Lena is kept from acting. While Jess loads all the Daxamite ship's information onto a private server and sets it to release if the invaders haven't been defeated within three days, Lena sets about making lead knuckles and a lead knife, because she has decided to kill Rhea to stop everything. Livewire says she's running away, and Lena agrees, saying she'd rather run from her problems and do some good than face them and let the world burn. When she gets back on the ship, she and Mon-El have a chat about family relationships; he thinks this is all Lena's fault, and Lena almost blames him (because, directly, it is sort of his fault), but ultimately settles on the real source of all this bullshit: Rhea. If Rhea had never made her, none of this would have happened.
Lena suits up as Galaxy Girl, because Galaxy Girl feels strong enough to do this when Lena feels weak, and because Galaxy Girl came into being to protect the citizens of Earth, independent of anyone else's greater plan - she belongs to the best of Lena, and that's who will win. Unfortunately, Lillian, Henshaw, and Kara show up to rescue her - and Kal-El. Lena finds out Kara knew what she was, and is too stunned to really process it. She and Kara are momentarily goopy and cute, and Lillian gets snide about it - is it because they got cute in Kryptonian, or because she finally figured out her daughter was gay? The world may never know. Anyways, Lillian and Henshaw leave without her, because she won't go, and Kara tries to talk Rhea down while Lena tries to rescue Kal-El, who, under the influence of Silver Kryptonite, thinks she's Kara. Kara challenges Rhea to Dakkam-Ur, and Rhea is about to accept, but Kal-El sees Zod attacking a civilian and decides It's Clobberin' Time. Lena convinces Rhea that Earth's dueling rites should be incorporated, realizing that when she gave Kara the ship's data, she inadvertently gave her the idea to battle a fascist warrior queen to the death. She meets with Alex, Lucy, and Kal-El to set up the time and place so Kara has the most advantages, warning them about the Kryptonite blood. Kal-El tells her that Lillian has an idea that could banish the Daxamites without a fight, but she's reluctant to use it; Lena wants to use it, but she doesn't have any lead left, having lost all of it in Kara and Rhea's fight on the ship, so she turns him down. Lucy is sort of horrified that she's 100% down to just... McFucking die for this. As Lena returns to the ship, she thinks she hears Alex apologize.

So, I knew this chapter was dense, but I just now realized how dense. Sorry about that. And the nearly two week gap between chapters. It's finals season at college, and I am... procrastinating through fanfiction, and then procrastinating that fanfiction through other fanfiction. It's a lot.

Anyways, I hope this chapter wasn't too much of a slog. This should be finished before Christmas; I recommend reading the last two chapters with some cinnamon hot chocolate and cookies, because 23 is going to hurt, and 24 is going to be fluffy as fuck. Feel free to yell at me in the comments.

23. Chapter 23

Summary for the Chapter:

Set during 2x22: Nevertheless, She Persisted. Come hell or high water, National City - and the world - will be safe.

Maybe she had, maybe she hadn’t. Lena didn’t have the time to think about what Alex said mid-transmat, or why she would possibly say it; the fate of humanity rested on her girlfriend’s shoulders.

It should have stayed on her own. 

In the hours of waiting, Lena paced the length of the ship more times than anyone could count. To Rhea’s credit, reluctant as anyone might be to give it to her, she didn’t interfere in Lena’s frenetic circling. As someone who saw her own husband die, maybe she understood the stakes. 

As someone who killed her husband to further her own ends, maybe she didn’t.

Either way, Lena’s pacing wasn’t just anxiety. No, as much as she would have liked to give in and be afraid, to drown in the nauseating swell of terror, she couldn’t let herself. 

Because, yes, Kara could probably defeat Rhea. Definitely. She was strong and fast and skilled and she had a reason to fight, a reason to win. The fucking fate of humanity depended on it. 

But Kara wanted to win for the same reason that winning would hurt her: because, deep in the heart of her, she was good. She didn’t kill. She stood for hope and help and compassion, not death, and from what Lena knew of her family history, there was better reason than most people had for her to walk that path. 

Lena, reluctant Daxamite, recalcitrant Luthor, understood that.

Which was why Lena was looking for her missing knife. 

Lost in the scuffle between Kara and Kal-El, the knife had to be somewhere. And if Lena could get her hands on it, if Lena could find it, if Lena could use it, then Kara wouldn’t have to do something that would hurt her so badly. 

Whether or not it hurt Lena was immaterial in her frenzy. Everything was immaterial but finding that goddamn lead-bladed knife and fixing that goddamn mess. 

After almost six hours of frantic, hyperkinetic, super-speed-walking, Lena still hadn’t found it.

Which meant someone else had. 

And she didn’t have time to find them, to steal the knife back, because, finally, after almost six hours, someone interrupted her pacing. 

“My Queen.” 

The guard was moving so slowly in comparison to Lena that she almost barreled right through him, catching herself just in time. 

“It is time.”

Lena’s breath caught, and her heart stopped, but she gave a jerky nod and followed him to the transmat. 

Rhea was wearing armor - insufficient, only over her torso - but then, she was probably banking on Kara injuring her badly enough to draw blood. Injury would be permissible if it resulted in her enemy’s defeat. 

It was probably a side effect of being largely invulnerable, but the whisper-thin voice in the back of Lena’s head was of the opinion that, maybe, just maybe, it wasn’t all aliens who felt that way. Maybe it was just Rhea, with her poison blood, and Lena, carrying lead with her bare hands. 

Mothers and daughters. Such a complicated relationship.

Rhea glanced Lena’s way fleetingly before nodding at the transmat technician, signaling that he should send them down, and down they went. 

They landed on one side of the D.E.O.’s rooftop. Standing opposite them was Kara, grimly determined and accompanied by Alex and, oddly enough, Winn. 

Once they landed, Alex started across the rooftop. Lena, fidgeting, peered past her as subtly as she could. 

Kara, under the squared jaw and the heroically akimbo stance, looked nervous. Winn reached over and grabbed her hand, giving it a gentle squeeze, and Kara’s shoulders softened infinitesimally. Only then did Lena move to meet Alex halfway. 

Before Alex could say a word, Lena’s fingertips began tapping on her thigh, just over the hip pocket of her suit. It was too arrhythmic to be a nervous tic, too fluid to be binary code. 

“Is everything ready?” she asked, as if nothing was amiss. 

Alex, focus split between decoding the Morse missive and responding, barely took a second to say, “Yes.” Then, she began to tap back: if you’re sure, we can quarantine a room with a circular air filter so you don’t get poisoned.

Lena’s jaw clenched, and she gave a tiny dissenting shake of her head, fingers fluttering against her leg. 

“Is Rhea ready to go?” Alex asked, ignoring Lena’s frantic spelling, tapping over her. I don’t know if Kara will do that to you.

This way, Lena spelled emphatically, with a sharp nod, she doesn’t have to do something worse.  

Alex let out a sigh through her nose and murmured, “I… hope it doesn’t come down to us.”

“Me, neither.”

Lena returned to Rhea’s side, for just a moment, to relay the message that the battle could begin, before departing. The laws of Dakkam-Ur were very clear on the matter of witnesses - save for the gods, there could be none.

As she, Winn, and Alex headed down, Lena wished she knew them well enough to call in a favor. Alex’s hand wrapped around her wrist, squeezing a gentle patternless tattoo: long-short-long-long, short, short-short-short.

Lena registered her meaning just in time for a bolt of heat to hit her square in the back of the neck. She managed not to stumble, but suddenly, everything was just so heavy.

“You okay, Legs?” Winn whispered, grabbing her arm, holding her steady. 

“I’m fine.” The hatch shut above their heads, and Lena pulled out of their grips, starting down the stairs. “We have to hurry.”

Chasing after her, Alex asked, “Did she really - ?”

“Yes,” Lena hissed. She stopped dead and turned, pinning her with her eyes. “I passed the transmat thousands of times, Alex. Last night, I called the troops back to the fleet, but she’s been sneaking them down all day. I clearly don’t have… pull enough to override her. They need an incentive to leave, and we’re going to give it to them.”

“Fine,” Alex said, settling her hands defiantly on her hips. “But I’m putting something on that.”

“On what?”

“The burn on the back of your neck.”

Lena reached back and touched the spot just under her skull she’d begun to treat as a sort of worry spot. Instead of the smooth hypertrophic lines left by Lillian’s aborted experimentation, there was a blooming blister that hurt like hell under her fingertips. Stalwartly suppressing a wince, Lena said, “Fine. But only if it doesn’t interfere with me working. This is more important - ”

“I am not letting you get an infection in your spine, Lena!”

“Then don’t get in my way.”

☆ 

Alex didn’t. Unobtrusive and efficient, it was clear to see that she would have made a great ER surgeon. She had the burn sterilized and iced in less time than it took for Lena and Winn to rejigger the inner workings of Lex’s atmospheric dispersal. 

Granted, Lena wasn’t working at full speed. It probably felt slower than it actually was, but that hadn’t even occurred to Lena. Her brain was running two programs: engineering and Mom argument.

Lillian stood in the doorway of the top floor lab, eyes hard and shiny. 

“If you want to blame me,” Lena said, staring up at her with her jaw set so tight it ached, “for what’s happening out there, go right ahead. I blame me, too. But if you want me to get this done, you need to let me work.”

Lillian took a step back, but it didn’t last, and soon she was back, looming over Lena’s space like she was six again, and painfully stupid, following her to the table bearing her own toolkit. “How could you let that woman deceive you? I taught you to be a scientist! To question everything!”

“No.” Lena grabbed a micro-welding torch, grip careful, voice sharp. “What you taught me was to doubt myself. To look for validation elsewhere, so much that I was willing to take it from the first mentor that offered it to me. There were warning signs that I ignored because I was so…” 

Her hands shook. She passed the torch over to Winn and rubbed her hands over the back of her neck, turning on her heel to look back at Lillian.

“Because I was so desperate for someone to love me, and be proud of me. To do good. To make up for everything you’ve done, Lex has done, Lionel did.” 

Those flinty eyes softened, for just a moment, and Lillian did something completely unprecedented: she apologized. And when Lena, rightfully incredulous, scoffed and tried to turn away, Lillian let her. She didn’t grab Lena and force eye contact, maybe even resisting the urge - her fingertips grazed the back of Lena’s wrist briefly before curling away.

Still, she insisted, “I am. When you came to visit me in jail, I honestly wanted to be a better mother to you. But every time I've had the opportunity to choose you over something else… I've chosen something else.”

“Well, congratulations on saying the first honest thing in your life.”

“I have justified the worst behavior for the best of causes,” Lillian ceded, “but I was right. The threat was real.”

“And I’m part of it.” Lena tried to pretend she was still strong with sunlight, squaring her jaw, but the way she tucked her hands away, making herself smaller - harder to touch - probably sold her out. “You can just - ”

“No! What I’m trying to say is, maybe I backed the wrong child to stop it.” 

The tiny corner of Lena’s heart that thirsted for that sentiment jerked her head upright, made her meet Lillian’s gaze. She didn’t look like she was lying, or saying something carefully carved of half-truths to reach her ends, and there was no hint of dishonesty in her voice as she continued, urgent and private.

“The transmat portal you created - that was brilliant, Lena. And if you could do that with the portal, maybe you could do something with this.”

Lillian presented her with the device, a small steel box, and Lena eyed it with eager trepidation, both wanting to take it and fix every mistake and wanting never to touch something Lex, something Lillian, something Luthor, ever again.

“Does it work?”

“Well, you’d need to adapt it. But if you could, you would be the Luthor who saved the world.”

The smallest, pettiest regret - the one at the top of Lena’s internal heap - was not taking the box sooner, so it couldn’t look like that was all that motivated her. 

Still, Lena took it, setting it down on the table next to her tools and Winn’s fidgety hands. “Unfortunately, this is her on her best behavior,” she quipped dryly.

“Hey,” Winn murmured, “you don’t have to apologize for her.”

Alex, standing across the table, had a hand on the butt of her blaster. “And you’re certain it’ll be safe for humans?”

“My son designed it to keep humans safe while making the planet uninhabitable for Kryptonians. If Lena can get it to work, it’ll make the atmosphere toxic for the Daxamites, instead. They would be forced to leave, or stay and die.”

Lena picked up her welding gloves, squeezing the tough material in her fists.

“So, you understand my… reservations.” And there was Lillian’s hand, perfectly proportionate to her statuesque frame, long-fingered and heavy on Lena’s shoulder. “Only if you’re sure.”

“It won’t hurt me,” Lena said, “if that’s what you’re angling for. Genes suppressed. I’m functionally human.”

“Good.”

Lena shrugged away and put on her gloves. She didn’t really need them, what with the ones built into her suit, but they helped her focus. If she had to finally feel how heavy things were, the metal plating of her armor dragging her bones down, she could at least choose how she bore it.

“If she tries anything,” Alex murmured, fingers meaningfully meaningless in their drumming on her gun.

As she opened the casing, Lena said nothing, doing her best to block out Lillian’s circling, Alex’s words, the brawl upstairs, audible even without superhearing. She and Winn worked as well as they had every other time they’d faced a problem shoulder to shoulder, and that was a comfort, in and of itself, but after a certain point, when the gloves came off, one question burned too brightly to ignore. 

“Did you know - ” Lena stopped, stacking them neatly and pushing them aside, bracing her hands on the edge of the table and, briefly, making herself look up at Alex. “Did you know Mon-El was my brother?”

Alex managed not to look away or radiate shame. “Yeah. Yeah, I did, and I’m - I’m sorry.”

“It’s fine.” Lena flashed a quick smile, waiting until Alex smiled back and let her shoulders loosen before she looked away. “Keeping secrets, right? To make each other happy?”

“Yeah.”

After that, things moved quicker. Lena and Winn passed the remote back and forth to each other in sync with Lillian’s circular pacing so she couldn’t see it, passing it across the table to Alex, who nodded covertly and tucked it away. All that was left then was to insert the lead core and activate it. 

It sat just beyond Winn’s elbow, totally innocuous. Lena swallowed around a lump in her throat and gestured vaguely, muttering, “Can I have the, uh, the - ?”

“Yeah.” Winn palmed it and passed it over with his bare hand. Like it was nothing. 

Lena swallowed again, peeling one hand free of her suit, and thanked him.

“You know, I’m pretty good in a crisis.”

Up above, something creaked dangerously, and dust and debris rained down on them - misted, really, but it was enough to make Winn yelp, to make Lena try and shield him, shove him aside. 

He barely moved. The two of them were sturdily built for a pair of nerds, but he was a lot heavier than an electron microscope, and she couldn’t budge him.

Briefly, Lena recalled when she’d been able to bodily lift him.

The crumbling stopped, and Lillian, who had been far from it thanks to her pacing, said, “We can see that.”

Winn wheeled, pointing a finger, and said, with false bravado, “I don’t like you.”

Lena, bare-handed, couldn’t quite make herself touch the lead. Maybe it was fear - fear she wasn’t strong enough to lift it, fear it might still burn her, fear it wouldn’t do a damn thing but confirm that she was weak again - but her fingers refused to curl closed. She slipped the suit’s glove back on, and her hand worked again, dropped the lead in with ease.

“It’s done.”

Lillian stopped pacing indiscriminately, barging right back over. “Turn it on,” she said, eyes bright. “We can end this.”

Winn, trying to pull it away from Lillian physically, also gave dissuading her his best shot, too. “Hey, no, no, no, wait! No, you can't do that.”

Lillian was never one to be dissuaded, and she shoved him aside without a hitch. Lena managed to catch him, but it was a strain, and Lillian managed to grab the disperser. 

Not before Alex made good on her promise, though, and pointed the blaster straight at her face. “Put. The box. Down.”

“There’s too much at stake to wait,” Lillian hissed, and pushed the lead core’s tower in, closing the box. 

To no avail.

“You said it worked.”

“It does.” Lena stood, pulling Winn to his feet. “But not for you.”

“Come on, get out of here.” Winn gave her hand a squeeze before letting go. “Get out of here, both of you. I can handle her.”

The quiet reminder that Winn came as close as anyone could to getting her family drama filled Lena with a steadying rush of gratitude, and she grabbed the dispersal and one baton, pressing it into his hand along with the controls. “Thank you.”

He smiled, nodded, and she and Alex ran for the rooftop.

“I really am sorry,” Alex said, pushing the hatch open. 

“And it’s really fine. You had your reasons - ”

“I was - you and Kara were so happy. I didn’t want anything to ruin that.” Alex paused, looking down at Lena. “There’s enough in your way without another blood feud.”

“And I appreciate it.” Lena stretched up and pushed with her, finally shifting the lid off so they could climb onto the roof. Before either of them could, there was a cry - Kara’s voice, twisted around pain.

At the same time, with the same horror, Alex and Lena whispered, “No,” and began to scramble. 

Rhea had crushed the anti-Kryptonite armor, casting it aside like dirty laundry and swatting Kara to the roof with it like she was a fly, a split in her eyebrow dripping glistening, glowing green.

“Did your blood - ?”

“No.” Lena boosted herself back onto the rooftop. “My tampons were a totally normal color.”

That green shine curled up Kara’s neck and cheek like old vines as she struggled to her knees, and Rhea swung an inelegant punch, blood glowing on her knuckles, that Kara managed to catch. Somehow, she held the fist, strong even in the face of her one weakness, and a desperate glint caught in Rhea’s eyes. 

“It won't stop here,” she promised. “There’s Star City, and Metropolis. I will destroy city after city until your whole world is gone.”

Kara’s face twisted, and she threw Rhea back into the ventilation intake fans, denting them, thankfully, not beyond repair. “This is my home. And I'm going to protect it.”

“It doesn't matter if I live or die,” laughed Rhea, tossing her head back. “We'll keep coming.”

Alex touched her earpiece, horror washing over her fine features like high tide. “They’ve got bogies on every school, hospital, and municipal building. They’re going to destroy everything.”

“No, they won’t.” 

Fingers light, heart heavy, Lena snatched the remote from Alex’s pocket and threw herself between Kara and the Queen, clutching the disperser to her stomach, shielding it as best she could. “Enough.”

“L’inah - ”

“No.” Slowly, Lena shook her head, gripping the remote. “You call them off, now, and maybe not every Daxamite dies today.”

“You - ” With a soft grunt, Rhea found her feet, wobbling towards Lena with a steady stride. “You wouldn’t hurt your own people, l’inah, not when you’ve sworn to protect them.”

“This is me, protecting my people.”

Rhea sighed, in the way only a disappointed mother can. “This is why you’re not ready to take control yet. You don’t understand - I’m not doing this to hurt you.”

“You hurt me,” Lena spat, “when you tried to kill the woman I love, when you tried to destroy my home.”

“This is not your home!” 

Alex drew her gun, aiming, the whine of the blaster’s charge filling the air. 

“Daxam was your home, until her kind destroyed it!”

“Earth is my home. You sent me here, to grow up, to assimilate. This planet is everything I’ve ever known, and it isn’t perfect, but it’s my home, and I promised to protect it.” Her throat clicked as she swallowed around what felt like a lump of hot lead. “How can you not love the people you protect?” 

“They’re not worthy - she’s not - !”

“You can be a casualty, or you can leave this place forever.”

“You don’t want that,” Rhea purred, stepping closer, arms outstretched. “You don’t want to kill me, to banish us, to be alone.”

“She’s not alone.” 

Only when Kara spoke, did Lena realize her hands had been steady on her hips, holding her up, the entire time.

“She’s not,” Kara repeated, more vehement, “and she will never be alone again.”

“L’inah,” Rhea tried, one last time, “I love you. I’m doing this, all of this, for you!”

“And that’s why you won’t stop. Because you love me.” Lena looked down, shifting her grip on the device, turning it over in her hands, glancing up at Rhea.

She was only a foot away, close enough to touch. 

Lena continued turning, counting hundredths in her head, until she hit the magic number - 59.04 degrees. Then, she finally looked her mother, the Queen, straight in the face, and said, “You should have run.”

Rhea’s hands closed around her forearms at the exact same moment the lead dispersed, blasting her right in the mouth and nose. The effect was instantaneous and horrible, and when she crumbled to dust, her hands were the last to go, clinging like cigar ash to Lena’s armor.

Kara twisted, shielding Lena and Alex from the blast in her cape. Alex murmured updates from the D.E.O. feed whenever they came, squeezing Lena’s hand, while Lena counted seconds until atmospheric dispersal was complete, and they could breathe easy. Even once the explosion had settled, though, and she knew she could retreat from Kara’s embrace, she didn’t. She burrowed closer, allowing herself to be swallowed up by loving arms and to hold onto someone as tight as possible without worrying about hurting them. 

She was tired, so tired, bone tired. Her limbs felt leaden from carrying the weight of her armor, and her head ached from that last brief moment of eye contact, and the burn scar on the back of her neck had grown. 

“You made sure it stayed off,” she murmured, resisting the urge to prod at the blistered flesh, “even when I looked at her.”

“Of course.” Kara kissed her temple. “I’m not going to let you get hurt, ever again.”

“C’mon. I gotta patch you up.”

Lena nodded, let Alex and Kara drag her to her feet and cart her inside. “What’s with you pointing guns at my moms today?”

“Privilege of being family, Legs: I get to shoot at your shit parents.”

Lena laughed, the nickname and the promise of family slicking down all the sharp edges of the past - had it really only been a few days?

Drowsily, she felt herself distantly hoping. The world had been saved. The battle for Earth had been won. Maybe things would be alright again.

Notes for the Chapter:

Not until the season's over and I have a chance to get shit done, but, yeah, it's already brewing, and everything is going to be addressed. To be honest, it was you guys being so supportive and wonderful that really convinced me - that, and the fact that I came up with a better crossover in five minutes while taking a study break before my last final. In the interim, though, I am going to try and A) take a step back by B) finishing and posting all of the WIPs currently floating around my hard drive, and not starting anything new for a while.
