Thank you so much for reading, and feel free to yell at me in the comments below. Merry Saturday!

24. Epilogue

Summary for the Chapter:

The beach day we were promised, complete with an adopted puppy, a Supergirl swimsuit, and some explanations.

“You ready to go?”

Lena looked up. There stood Kara, fidgeting in her doorway.

Their doorway.

Lena’s apartment, bordering the northernmost edge of the financial district, had been wrecked in the attack. It was as good an excuse as any to move in with Kara; she spent all her time before the invasion there anyway, and it was better than staying in a hotel.

Better than being alone.

When they found out, Kara had pulled her into a hug and said, “I love you, Lena. Anything I can do.”

They did that a lot. Saying they loved each other. It felt good.

“Yeah. Just - one - second.” Lena saved her open code and stood, popping her neck.

“Ooh!” Kara zipped over. “Careful!”

“I’m fine. Scar didn’t rupture.” Lena, mid-wave off, draped her arms around Kara’s shoulders and kissed her. “You worry.”

“So do you, Ms. Clean Up Crew.”

The monicker was accurate, if embarrassing. Not much was wrecked by the invasion, but what has been destroyed has been put back together with L Corp money and Lena Luthor’s blood, sweat, and time. 

Supergirl had been helping out, too. Part of the territory.

“Yeah, well…” Lena shrugged. “Today’s a worry-free day, right?”

Kara beamed, sunny-warm, and kissed her forehead. “Right. C’mon. Bags are packed, wheels up in three.”

“Three?” Lena wrinkled her nose. “That’s such an arbitrary number.”

“All numbers are arbitrary, i zhor, they’re numbers. That’s, like, seventy percent of the fun.”

“You’re seventy percent of the fun.” Lena closed her laptop and tugged on her sandals. “We’re driving?”

“Alex commandeered a vehicle - ”

“ - meaning J’onn is pudding since M’gann came back - ”

“ - so she’s driving.” Kara laughed. “But yeah.”

“I can’t believe we’re going to the beach,” muttered Lena, “in the rain.”

“You love the rain. You’re always saying you miss weather!”

Another accurate statement. Lena was just… leery of that weather, caused by atmospheric disturbances in the vein of spaceship entry and exit, precipitation full of Pb. 

Not full enough to hurt her as a human, and she wasn’t Daxamite enough to be harmed at such low levels, but it was the principle of the thing. Anxiety’s a bitch like that.

And so what if Lena’s been a little more anxious since the invasion, and all that it entailed? She’s got people, people who love her and support her. People who will commandeer a vehicle just to drive her to the beach, because a vacation day came highly recommended.

“See, when you said D.E.O.,” Lena began, eyes appreciatively wide as they gobble up the powder blue ’52 Chevy Deluxe, “I pictured… slick black SUV. Creepy truck.”

“Ha! No.” Alex grinned from the driver’s seat of the convertible, draping one arm over the door. Her other hand was in Maggie’s lap, scratching behind the ears of a familiar pit bull puppy.  Gigantor - now Gertrude - looked perfectly cozy in her new mom’s lap, licking her nose lazily, tail wagging. “No, this baby is J’onn’s, and if I scratch it, death befall us, so lids on drinks, pants on legs, etcetera, etcetera.”

“And towels on the seat?”

Maggie winked from the passenger side, aiming a truly spectacular finger gun Kara’s way. “Bingo, little Danvers.”

“Hop in. We gotta get rolling.”

Kara hopped in, and Lena followed suit, sliding over the top of the door and crashing, with spectacular clumsiness, into her girlfriend’s lap. Kara helped tug her all the way into the convertible, wrapping her arms around Lena’s waist and burying her face in her hair. “Mm. Road trip.”

“Road trip!” Alex hollered, and they peeled out of park and into the remarkably empty street. The radio crackled to life, an improbable Throwback Thursday on a still-dark Saturday morning, and Lena grinned, ear to ear. 

“I love this song,” she laughed. 

“You’re not gay if you don’t love the Spice Girls,” Maggie fired back, scraping her hair up into a ponytail. “Yo, tell you what I want, what I really, really want!”

“So tell me what you want, what you really, really want!”

“Alex! Hands on the wheel,” Kara insisted, “we don’t have seat belts in this - zig-a-zig-ah!”

Lena caught a glimpse of her face in the rearview mirror. She was smiling like an idiot, a few strands of shower-wet hair clinging to her ruddy cheeks, driving over smooth pavement with her girlfriend’s arms acting as the best kind of seatbelt. 

Yeah, she thought, things are okay.

“If you want my future - ”

“Yes!”

“ - forget my past!”

“If you wanna get with me, better make it fast!”

“So don’t go wastin’ my precious time,” Alex crooned, melody dropping off as the stop light ahead flickered directly to red from green. “Aw, come on! Get your act together, you stupid street light!”

Lena cackled, wondering if it was Livewire or a genuine infrastructure problem. Hopefully, she and Jess were back on vacation; it may have only been a few days since the invasion’s end, but there was no saying whether or not they could afford to stick around.

Still, it was nice to think about. Lena still couldn’t believe that Livewire had been down in the streets, fighting back with everyone else, blowing out Daxamite staves and blasters. For all her villainous claims, she was, at worst, a sort of chaotic anti-hero, and Lena was glad of it.

National City needed all the help it could get. 

Kara, as if she could smell the introspection a mile away, kissed her temple, singing, “I'll tell you what I want, what I really, really want! So, tell me what you want, what you really, really want! I wanna, huh, I wanna, huh, I wanna, huh - ”

Lena, giggling, leaned into Kara’s arms, focusing in on that instead of anything else. Sure, she still had shit to do to fix up the city, but the roads were clear and smooth, utilities were still running, and no one was sleeping on the streets. Everyone in the city was taking a day off for the weekend, because everyone in the city had earned it.

“ - really, really, really wanna zig-a-zig-ah!”

“Hey, Kar,” Alex called from the driver’s seat, shit-eating grin plastered across her face. “Kar. Remember when I told you that was an actual word on Earth?”

“Remember when you thought you only had that music video recorded on VHS because you liked the song?” Kara fired back.

Alex stuck out her tongue in the rearview mirror, and Kara heartily responded, jaw flexing against Lena’s temple. 

“Ladies, ladies, there’s no need to seduce us,” Maggie drawled. “We’re already running away with you.”

Alex laughed in the goofy, giddy way she always did when Maggie made a joke, like Maggie was the funniest fucking person to ever draw breath, and Kara murmured, “Nyoom,” in Lena’s ear to make her giggle, too. 

Through her laughter, Lena said, “Not running. Just - taking a break.”

“No.” Kara’s thumb caressed the curve of Lena’s waist through her borrowed hoodie, spreading goosebumps over her skin like soft butter on hot toast. “Heroes don’t run from anything.”

Lena smiled, a little unsure, down at her knees and sang, “Zig-a-zig-ah.”

☆

The beach was mostly unoccupied, save for a few close friends. Winn and James had driven out in their van, though the lead-lined helmet and headset were safely stowed away, and J’onn and M’gann had flown there together. M’gann shifted immediately into her humanoid skin, and it was actually pretty funny to see her in an athletic one piece and cape before the last vestiges of her true form faded out, but J’onn stayed green a little longer, just staring out at the beach. 

“I’ve always liked this,” he said thoughtfully, staring out at the lapping grey waves. “All the water on Mars is frozen. The first time I saw liquid water, I was utterly amazed.”

“It is beautiful,” Maggie agreed. “I grew up smack-dab in the middle of the Midwest, but then I moved to Metropolis. Right on the beach.”

“East Coast beaches,” Lena said with a smile, and Maggie knocked their shoulders together. “California water’s not bad.”

Alex, in her shorts and surf shirt, had finally convinced Kara to launch her into the water. She cleanly speared through the waves without so much as a splash, then bobbed up with a gasp, hair slicked back, water sluicing down around her eyebrows. 

“Not bad at all.”

Lena laughed at the atrociously obvious case of heart eyes she was sporting for her girlfriend - fiancée, she reminded herself, glimpsing the ring on Maggie’s finger as it glittered in the muted sun - then waved her off towards the water. “Dive in after your lady.”

“You coming?”

“Can’t.” Lena touched the bandage on the back of her neck, prodding briefly. Still hurt. “Doctor’s orders; can’t risk infection.”

Sympathetic, Maggie nodded, clapping her on the shoulder, then raced off into the surf, launching herself onto Alex and tackling her below the waves with a giddy yelp. Lena found herself grinning, arms crossed low over her belly in a haphazard hug, and thinking It’s nice to see people so happy, after. 

“It is,” J’onn said, green face melting into brown. “Like the world is telling you that healing can happen.”

Suddenly conscious of the observation, Lena’s hands curled a little tighter around her waist. “Any sign of - ?”

“No. Everyone is gone. Mon-El sent a message, promising he’d keep them at bay.”

“Good.”

“You can listen to it, if you’d like.”

“I just might.” Lena nodded slowly. “Thank you, J’onn.”

“It’s the least we can do.”

M’gann shot Lena a look, soft and grateful, after stretching up and kissing J’onn’s cheek, face cradled in her hands. “Come on,” she murmured. “Alex promised she would teach us how to surf.”

“I’ve been on this planet three hundred years,” J’onn said, affecting disgruntlement but already following her. “If I wanted to surf, I would have done it by now.”

M’gann was, perhaps, less subtle in her machinations to give Lena some space, but that was part of what made it nice. She wasn’t being left, just respected.

Lena thought her thanks M’gann’s way, then headed back up the beach to where Winn was dangling his legs out the back of the van and James was toeing off his sandals. 

“Hey.”

“Hey!”

“Mind if I join?”

“Not at all, Legs.” Winn scooted over, patting the bare metal beside him. “Hop on up!”

Hop up Lena did, feet swinging, tossing James’ shoes back into the vehicle so they didn’t collect any more sand than necessary. “No Lyra today?”

“She and, uh, her little brother needed a family day.” Winn smiled, a little crooked, and ruffled his own hair. “Which I totally get. After… everything.”

“Yeah. I’ve been, um.” Lena ran her fingers through her hair, fingertips skimming over her bandage. “I’ve been thinking. Maybe I should - maybe I should pop by Stryker Island.”

“Yeah?” James leaned against the hinge of the back door, smoothing his palm over the top of his head. “If you want some company, I’m always down for a road trip and real pizza.”

“What’s this I hear about real pizza?”

Out from around the van came Lucy Lane, all jean shorts and oversized sunglasses, with Vasquez in tow. James grinned, and they each pulled each other into a hug hello.

“Um.” Lena smiled in greeting. “We might be planning a road trip, is all. Nostalgia tour of the Northeast.”

“Head up in, like, October or something. Get weather, but drivable weather.”

Lena laughed. “How is it that we’re in California, and yet only two of the people here are actually from California?”

Vasquez cackled. “Right! Me and Al are the only ones! The rest of you are, what, Jersey, Jersey, Jersey, Jersey, space, space, space?”

Counted amongst the four, Lena grinned, wider and more genuine. “It may be the Garbage State,” she said proudly, “but it’s my Garbage State.”

“I’ll drink to that!” Lucy whooped, extracting a six-pack from the admittedly impressive oversized tote bag hanging off her shoulder. “And, yes, it is six in the morning, but I have been awake for the past two days, so my internal clock is ringing Happy Hour.”

Lena, equally thus, shrugged and grabbed a Blue Moon, trying to twist the cap off. The fluted metal dug harshly into her palm, and she flinched before tugging her sleeve down over her hand and trying again. 

“Wimp,” Lucy teased, knocking the cap off against the door.

“Not all of us can digest broken glass, Lane,” Vasquez ribbed right back, twisting her cap off with her bare hand. 

“I have whiny baby skin,” sniffed Lena. 

“To Lena’s whiny baby skin, then.” Lucy clinked their bottles together with a wink before taking a sip. “Mm. Breakfast of champions.”

“See, you kid, but beer built the pyramids.” Winn, the kind of person who kept a bottle opener on his keys, used it for himself and then James, who didn’t even have to ask before his man in the van popped the top for him. “Liquid bread.”

Lena tried very hard to think about how no new pyramids had been built, and how that was a success - a good thing. She took a sip of her beer and tucked her feet up into the van, resting them on her knees lotus-style. Lucy laid out a towel where Lena’s feet had been, then plopped down on it, tugging Vasquez down to sit next to her, leaning up against the hung-ajar door of the van. 

“There’s no point, you know. It’s raining. You’ll get all wet and sandy, anyways.”

Lucy flexed her ankles, popping the joints with impressive grotesqueness, and buried her toes in the sand. “Free exfoliation.”

With a snicker, James sat down on Winn’s other side, their knees knocking together, and sipped his beer. Winn blinked like a bug had flown in his face, but after a moment, he settled back down, squinting up at the cloud-cloaked sun. 

“Nice, uh.” He took a swig, wiping his mouth on the back of his wrist. “Nice day.”

Overhead, the dark clouds seemed to darken in response, the rain coming down harder. 

“You people are weird,” Vasquez muttered, flicking Winn’s kneecap. 

“Ah!” drawled James, nudging Winn’s shoulder with his elbow, “we have our charm.”

Lena gazed out at the ocean, at Alex attempting to teach quadricentennial aliens and one stubborn cop to surf while Kara skimmed over the water’s surface like a dragonfly, kicking up a mist in her wake that caught the dull light and cast brief arcs of iridescence. 

“Yeah,” she said with a candle flame smile. “We do.”

☆

Kara zoomed over, hovering parallel to the sand just to give Lena a kiss hello. Her hands braced lightly on Lena’s shoulders, more warmth than weight, and her voice sounded like that, too, when she murmured, “Hi,” noses and foreheads knocking together.

“Hi,” Lena replied, raking her fingers through Kara’s curls. “Enjoying yourself?”

“Yeah. You? You’re not lonely up on the sand?”

“Nah.” Shaking her head, Lena draped one hand over Kara’s shoulder, absently stroking the coil of her trapezius. “I’m good up here.”

“Yeah?”

Lena nodded and kissed Kara again. “Promise.”

A goofy sort of look crossed Kara’s face and she floated down into Lena’s lap, straddling her thighs and beaming. “Well, I’m pooped. Mind if I laze around up here for a while?”

Knowing for a fact that there was no way in hell Kara was tired, Lena smiled just as wide and lovestruck and said, “Not at all.”

The sun was about at its peak, still concealed by a thick cloud cover, but when Lena closed her eyes and tilted her face into it, she felt the full extent of its warmth. She didn’t allow herself to wonder whether or not it felt different now, hooking her chin over Kara’s shoulder and clinging to the ropy muscle around her waist. 

Kara, for her part, clung back, fists tight in the fabric of Lena’s hoodie, nose tucked into the join of her neck and shoulder. She held on lie she was afloat in unknown waters and Lena was the only driftwood for miles, the only thing holding her up. The way Kara held her made Lena’s heart pound in her chest, and she opened her blurry eyes to look up at the yellow sun above them.

“I love you.”

“I love you, too.”

After about ten minutes, it became clear that Kara was still floating, because Lena’s legs hadn’t gone numb under her weight. It was thoughtful, considerate, and left a funny sort of weight in Lena’s chest. On wicked impulse, Lena rocked sideways, toppling them over so now it was she who sat square in her girlfriend’s lap, kneeling between her thighs. “You,” she said, tapping the tip of Kara’s nose, “are the absolute best.”

Kara’s face was spectacularly pink, the color of a truly atrocious sunburn, and if not for the fact that she couldn’t burn based off Kryptonian biology and would probably only tan if she were human, Lena would have suspected that’s what it was. Knowing better, though, Lena smiled crookedly and pulled her Oxford hoodie off overhead.

Kara moved to adjust her glasses, only to remember with her fingers on the bridge of her nose that she wasn’t wearing them. Her cheeks were now practically the same burgundy as Lena’s discarded sweatshirt, blue eyes bright and glassy. “You…”

“Number one fan.”

It seemed Kara had already forgotten her glasses were back at their apartment, because there she was, trying to adjust them, staring at - if Lena was to be polite - her Supergirl swimsuit. 

“It was why you decided we had to go to the beach,” she drawled, taking Kara’s hand and kissing her fingertips. 

“Only a week late.”

It was hard to reconcile, sometimes, that the whole mess had taken less than a week. The city had been under repair for less than a week, the Daxamite fleet had been gone for less than a week, Galaxy Girl had been dead for less than a week, and less than a week ago, Kara had switched the gene suppressor back on, rendering Lena effectively human. 

Lena had been working too hard to have the chance to really miss her powers. Public reconstruction meant, even if she still had them, she couldn’t have used them. And sure, she was tired in a way she hadn’t been since the suppressor failed, and she wasn’t healing as fast, and she wasn’t as strong, but Lena had worked hard not to give that a second thought. There was too much to do to spare a moment for mourning.

Kara had, in her own unsubtle way, tried to signal that Lena could do it, anyway, but Lena preferred being busy to being sad. 

“There are worse things to be late for,” Lena said firmly. “And we have the beach all to ourselves.”

Hands settling warm on Lena’s hips, Kara ducked down, eyelids heavy, going in for what would probably have been one hell of a kiss. 

Their lips had barely brushed when there was a yelp and a splash, and they both jerked away, peering towards the water.

All was well; a game of chicken comprised of four secret agents, one police officer, and one vigilante CEO with biceps like boulders was never going to end without someone getting wet. 

“I’m okay!” Winn hollered.

“That’s what you get for picking the tallest guy here,” Lena yelled down the beach. “Your center of gravity’ll fuck you over every time!”

“Goddamnit, gravity!”

Kara snickered, forehead thudding into Lena’s collarbone, and Lena couldn’t help but laugh, too. Things may have been heavy, but little things like that made them lighter. 

We’re going to get through this just fine, she said to herself.

Gertrude scampered up the beach, too-big paws and too-long legs kicking up sand in a series clumsy sprays. She launched herself up into the van, scrambling to actually make it in until Kara boosted her up and smooched her forehead. 

“Hi, baby!” she crooned.

Gertrude grinned a dumb puppy grin and licked Kara’s chin, and Kara laid back, letting the puppy sprawl out on her chest. 

Lena scratched Gert’s back, noticing just how much bigger the littlest of her litter had gotten under Alex and Maggie’s care. As Gert hunkered down on Kara’s sternum, tail practically a blur with how fast it was wagging under four hands’ worth of back scratches, Lena found herself smiling, too, thinking, Yeah. We’re gonna be fine.

☆

They hadn’t exactly intended to spend a whole day at the beach, or maybe Lena just hadn’t thought the math through, but soon enough, it was dark out, and Kara was insisting on starting a bonfire. 

“I can fly out, grab marshmallows, blast some driftwood, and have us rolling in s’mores in under a minute.”

“No need to fly, Supergirl,” James ribbed, nudging Kara’s shin with the side of his foot. “Winn keeps so much junk food in the van, Willy Wonka cries himself to sleep at night.”

“When Wonka makes kosher marshmallows, he can stop crying.”

“And we can start a fire without superpowers.” Maggie, who had already started collecting driftwood, plonked down in the sand and shot her soon-to-be-sister-in-law a look. “If today is a day off, that means for you, too.”

“Hey!”

Lena, legs draped over Kara’s lap, gave her cheek a pat and a quick kiss before sliding into the sand next to Maggie. “We’re an industrious bunch,” she protested. “I’m certain we can handle this sans heat vision.”

Kara resigned herself to waiting for her industrious companions to light driftwood on fire, hanging back and chattering quietly with M’gann, occasionally poking someone in the shoulder with her toe just to get an indignant giggle out of them. 

Eventually, they had a fire pit underway, crackling with pretty purplish flames, and a lazy s’more assembly line had formed. Someone had to roast marshmallows, break graham crackers and chocolate bars, divy up pieces, put things together, and keep Gertrude away from the chocolate. Alex, despite having been the first to protest risking melty marshmallow and sand as a team-up, ended up volunteering for sandwich duty, parking herself next to Lena, who was singularly adept at toasting marshmallows without burning them.

“So,” she said, quietly, smearing marshmallow between two graham cracker halves, “you probably already know this. Probably ran the numbers yourself.”

Lena asked, “What numbers?” with a perfectly neutral curiosity.

“Ten days.” Alex passed the s’more back to Maggie, who kissed her on the cheek before taking a bite. “For particulate lead to leave the atmosphere and be flushed into the topsoil. Probably less time under these circumstances, since all the upper atmo activity basically has us living in Atlantis.”

Saying nothing, Lena speared a new batch of marshmallows and lowered them over the fire. 

“But, just to be safe, ten days.” Alex let out a heavy breath. “Until it’s safe to power up again. If you were thinking about it.”

“Thanks, Alex.”

“And we can - we can do it in the med bay, no laser x-ray tag teaming.”

“Thank you, Alex.”

Alex sort of stiffened beside Lena, digging her toes into the sand, and a flare of guilt lit Lena up inside.

“No, it’s - I really do appreciate it. I just - ” Lena shifted her marshmallows into one hand and reached over, giving Alex’s knee a squeeze. “I don’t know if there’s a point. Galaxy Girl is - is ruined, now, for the public, and I don’t exactly have a secret identity anymore. Plus, after everything…”

I don’t know if people will trust someone with Daxamite powers.

“You got Ms. Grant’s email, right?”

There was Kara, charming and guileless even as she eavesdropped, planting a kiss on the crown of Lena’s head and handing over another broken-up chocolate bar. 

“About, um, interviewing me.”

“Yeah. She thinks it might help - ”

“Minimize blowback, both personal and professional. Protect everyone employed at L Corp.”

“And protect you.”

“It’s a good idea.” Lena rotated the marshmallows, inspecting for color, and passed them Alex’s way. “I told her I’d do it.”

“Yeah?”

Lena nodded, twisting back to kiss Kara’s cheek. “Yeah. Cat’s - I’ve known her since I was a teenager, you know? She worked at the Planet, Kal-El had ties to the Planet through James and Lois and…” She smirked, arching an eyebrow. “I was actually looking forward to sharing airspace with her again when I moved out here. If anyone besides Kara Danvers is interviewing me, I’m glad it’s her.”

Even with the excuse of firelight, Kara’s face was warm. 

“Once reconstruction is finished, she and I will have a chat,” Lena promised. “Thank you for arranging it.”

“Actually, Cat already had the idea when I presented it to her.”

Huh.

“She remembers you the same way you remember her, I guess. She said it was unfortunate that she left right when you arrived.”

“Yeah.”

☆

Everyone starts off home, piece by piece. Gertrude conked out around the second round of s’mores, and Alex and Maggie had to take their poor puppy home. Winn and James were next, saying their goodbyes around ten with familiar full-force hugs, and then M’gann flew off to pick up J’onn’s car and drive her back to the D.E.O.

Vasquez dragged Kara off on recycling duty, and that should have been the first clue. It was just J’onn and Lucy, the two directors, sitting around the dying fire with Lena. 

Lucy pulled her phone out of her shorts and passed it to Lena. “You should see this.”

Resigned to her fate, Lena stared down at the screen. A recorded video transmission was waiting to be played.

Mon-El’s face, twisted up in the same expression as is often seen on a child reluctant to go to the dentist but knowing there’s no way around it, stared up at her from beneath the play button.

Lena glanced up at J’onn, at Lucy, fingers resisting the command to press. “Is it - ?”

“Not a threat. But it’s something you should know.”

Not a threat. Not a threat.

Lena pressed play.

“Hello,” Mon-El said. He was in a cockpit, piloting what only took Lena a split second to recognize as Rhea’s ship. “I’m, uh, I’m taking point right now, leading everyone away. There’s an uninhabited planet with a yellow sun, water - everything we need. I thought, um, I thought maybe I could make a fresh start there, but…” He sighed, shifting in his seat. “Kara was right. I have a chance to fix things. My history isn’t just history, and I can - change things. Make things better.”

Lena set the phone down on her knees, which were draped in her sweatshirt like a blanket, so she could watch without touching. 

“And, um, she was right, too.” Mon-El scratched the side of his neck, eyes cutting down and to the left. “The Luthor. Was right. So I’m - I’m not running. Or, I am, but they’re all running with me. I’m gonna try - try and change things. No more - no more drugs, no more slaves, no more caste system. I’m going to be the leader they deserve. The kind of leader who can be proud of what he’s done.

“So you don’t - you don’t have to worry about them, about us coming back. Earth earned its freedom, and I’ll make sure no one interferes with that.” He laughed, a little sharp, a little bitter. “No way I’m gonna let them be right. And they’ll probably never see this, so… so I can say that it’s probably a good thing neither of them liked me much. Otherwise they wouldn’t have called me out, and I would have just… run off and let the Earth die. Let my people die.

“I - I think that’s it. Don’t tell them I said anything nice.”

He said something nice?

“Mon-El, King of Daxam until he can install a democratic voting system, out.”

And with that, the transmission ended. 

“Naturally, we trust him about as far as I can throw him,” Lucy said, taking her phone back and stretching her legs out, heels digging deep furrows in the sand, “but seeing as he’s thrown himself into a galaxy far, far away…”

“And we have a satellite array in the upper atmosphere that will identify incoming crafts based on design origin, energy source, and prior associations,” J’onn listed, leaning his elbows on his knees, making eye contact with Lena over the fire. “If he reneges, he won’t even make landfall before he gets punted into prison.”

“Oh,” said Lena mildly, “good.” When neither Director’s eyes left her, still scrutinizing, still concerned, she tacked on, “Is that all?”

“Um, yeah. He’s gone for good, we’re safe, and that’s a killer bikini.”

“That wasn’t in the transmission.”

“And thank god.”

Lena cracked a smile at Lucy’s dramatic tone. “Okay. Well, thank you for letting me know. That’s…” She sighed. “That’s a weight off. Thank you.”

“Of course, Agent Luthor.”

Lena blinked, much the same way Winn had when James had mentioned charm, like something had flown into her face for a split second. “Wait, Agent?”

“Of course.” J’onn smiled, eyes crinkling; the fire popped, spitting sparks into the sky. “Your protective suspension has been lifted.”

“But I’m - I’m not - ”

“You’re smart, you’re skilled, and you’ve been combat trained. No different from any other field agent or analyst on staff.”

“Thank you, J’onn. I won’t let you down.”

“You haven’t yet.”

Kara and Vasquez plodded towards them like an overexcited golden retriever on a strict leash and the person holding it until Lucy yelled, “Hey, hot stuff!” Then Vasquez laughed and unwound her arm from Kara’s, releasing her to zoom across the beach and scoop Lena up with an arm under her knees and another at her back.

“Oh, my god!”

“You sound happy,” Kara said, nodding towards Lena’s sternum. “Good news?”

The sea, glazed in moonlight, blurred by beneath them, and Lena tightened her arms around Kara’s neck. “Yeah. Mon-El is going off to his hideaway planet, and he’s bringing the fleet with him. Turns out nothing fuels a frat boy like girls yelling at him; he’s gonna try and actually fix things.”

“Well, that’s good.”

“And I’m off suspension.”

Kara let out a whoop, barrel-rolling over the surf, and Lena laughed. 

“That’s incredible, and I’m so proud of you, and I love you, love you, love you!”

“Khap rrip zhao.”

Kara grinned, wide and slow, and tugged Lena closer, slowly tilting upwards until her feet dangled in the water, but Lena was safely out of the waves’ reach. “You’re the best, you know that?”

Lena’s mouth twisted, bottom lip caught in her teeth. 

“I’m serious. You sacrifice so much, and you work so hard, and I’m - in awe of you.”

“Pot, kettle, Supergirl.” Lena swung her legs out of Kara’s grasp, dangling from her shoulders and staring her straight in the face. “I could never have done half the stuff I’ve done this past year without you. We’re a team, and I wouldn’t have it any other way.”

Kara scoffed, tightening her arms around Lena’s waist, eyes bright. “I’m - I know Alex told you the timeline - ”

“Yeah. I have about a week until it’s safe to switch my powers back on.”

“Well, whatever decision you make, I’m with you. One hundred percent.”

“Thanks.” Lena curled her fingers into Kara’s hair, running them through the flight-born tangles. “And thank you for turning them off. Alex thought it would be hard for you, and I - I appreciate it.”

“I couldn’t let you die.”

“It all goes back, though, doesn’t it? To that stupid scanner.”

“I guess it does. Same technique, different application.” Kara wrinkled her nose. “Did I ever apologize for frying your scanner?”

“You don’t need to.”

“I want to.”

“Too bad,” Lena said. “You’re not apologizing for anything you did, okay?”

“But - ”

Lena shook her head. 

“Fine. No apologizing.” Kara dipped lower, waves lapping at her ankles. “Can I - ?”

“No! You didn’t do anything you need to apologize for. I am fine.”

“You don’t have to be.”

“You’re sweet to be so concerned, but I really am fine.” A plan, half-cocked and foolhardy, formed in Lena’s head, and she grinned before letting go of Kara, dropping into the water up to waist. 

Kara’s eyes widened. “Your - ”

“It’s way out of the water,” drawled Lena, resolutely not touching the back of her neck, instead propping her hands on her hips. “You can stop worrying about me.”

“Fat chance.” Grinning, Kara floated down, crossing her legs and hovering just above the surface of the waves. “I like you too much for that.”

“Oh,” Lena teased, cocking her hip, “you like me.”

Kara shrugged coyly, draping her arms around Lena’s neck. “Sure do.”

“Do you like me enough to fly us home?”

“I like you enough to do a whole lot more than that.”
